reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining the OneCoin business through recruitment and presents rapid network growth, very large turnover, and extraordinary personal earnings as evidence of the opportunity. The speaker explicitly highlights building a large downline, describes creating the compensation and reward plans, and the description directs viewers to learn about the business and become members. These claims and the recruitment call to action form an earnings-dependent hierarchy rather than neutral reporting or ordinary cryptocurrency commentary.

citations.quote: Recruiting members throughout Thailand.
I still have a world record to building the biggest fastest downline in two companies.
I did the compensation plan, I did the reward plan.
Every day turnover 1.2 million euros.
How many? Nobody of you will say no to money?

opening.argument: The presentation itself engages with the possibility that viewers may hear accusations of fraud, rather than concealing that controversy. The speaker acknowledges that searches may call OneCoin a scam and challenges the judge to compare that kind of label with similar claims about established network businesses. He also expressly rejects the characterization of the activity as a money game and calls it real business. That is a contested public discussion with an explicit denial, not a one-sided promise of guaranteed success. The available material therefore supports treating the video as an attempt to explain and defend a disputed business model, with viewers able to assess the competing claims.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats every business figure as solicitation, but it does not establish that the speaker guaranteed an individual's earnings or concealed controversy. Its selected recruitment quote comes from the description, while the spoken material directly addresses the accusation that the activity is a money game and disputes it. A disputed explanation should not automatically be treated as deceptive promotion merely because it discusses growth and compensation.

citations.quote: Is this a money game? No.
no this is real business

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the activity real business is an unsupported assertion, not a risk warning or meaningful disclosure. The presentation still foregrounds rapid member growth, turnover, and a compensation plan while the description explicitly says it is recruiting members. Comparing OneCoin with other companies does not answer whether this particular opportunity depends on recruitment or whether its claims are substantiated.

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be understood as a news-style or explanatory account of the speaker's experience and the company's claimed development. The title itself identifies the item as news, while the speaker says he will explain the story of OneCoin, his own role, and the company's vision. He discusses how the project began, who was involved, and the claimed growth figures. That is commentary about a cryptocurrency venture and its reported scale, not proof that the video certifies every claim or guarantees an outcome to every viewer. The presence of a presentation setting and projected dashboard is also consistent with an informational business talk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side infers the video's purpose from isolated business vocabulary, but the supplied title calls it news and the spoken opening frames it as a story about the speaker and the company's vision. Describing a compensation plan or reporting claimed growth does not by itself prove that the entire presentation is an earnings-dependent hierarchy. The record does not supply the actual membership process or terms.

citations.quote: onecoin news from JUHA thank you Khun Fon
I'm going to tell you the story about OneCoin.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A news label supplied by the uploader cannot override what the content promotes. The speaker says he created the compensation and reward plans, describes a downline, and reports explosive membership and turnover figures. Those are not merely neutral market observations: they present the opportunity's network structure and performance as reasons to take it seriously. The description then directs viewers to learn about the business and become members.

citations.quote: I still have a world record to building the biggest fastest downline in two companies.
I did the compensation plan, I did the reward plan.
Interested in becoming a member? Click ...

opening.argument: Even taking the promotional context at face value, the supplied evidence does not show the core mechanics needed to classify this as a scam rather than a business or service promotion. The description invites people to learn about a business and become members, but it does not show a payment, deposit, credential request, guaranteed return, or promised individual payout. The frames show speakers presenting on a stage with a projected dashboard, not a transaction or enrollment screen. The spoken claims concern a cryptocurrency company, coins, and reported business turnover. Recruitment language alone does not establish that money comes from an unlawful or guaranteed-return mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side labels the arrangement a hierarchy without identifying any supplied term requiring payment, promising a return, or paying income for a particular recruit. It relies on the words downline and compensation plan, but those terms can occur in legitimate sales organizations. The available frames likewise show a public presentation, not a transaction or enrollment process.

citations.quote: I still have a world record to building the biggest fastest downline in two companies.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing transaction details do not erase the mechanism that is actually shown. The description explicitly recruits members, and the speaker links success to a large downline while saying he designed the compensation and reward plans. The video also emphasizes member counts and turnover as evidence of the opportunity. Those facts support a recruitment-based earnings structure even without a visible payment screen or individualized guarantee.
